name: Squash rules summary
summary: Two players share an enclosed four-walled court and take turns hitting the ball so that it reaches the front wall above the tin before it bounces twice on the floor. Every rally scores a point, games go to 11 with a two-point lead needed from 10-all, and a match is usually the best of five games.

points.text: The server drops or throws the ball and hits it straight to the front wall, between the service line and the out-line, with one foot on the floor inside the service box and not touching its lines; the ball must then land in the opposite quarter-court (the back quarter on the receiver's side) without touching a line, unless the receiver volleys it
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 5.7

points.text: The server picks a service box at the start of each game and whenever the serve changes hands, then alternates boxes for as long as they keep winning rallies
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 5.2

points.text: There is no second serve: a serve that breaks Rule 5.7 is a fault and the receiver wins the rally
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 5.8

points.text: A serve that touches the service line, the short line, the half-court line or any out-line counts as a fault
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 5.8, Note

points.text: If a rally ends in a let, the server serves again from the same box
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 5.3

points.text: The player who wins a rally scores one point and serves next, whoever served
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 2.1

points.text: A game is played to 11 points; from 10-all it continues until one player is two points ahead
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 2.2

points.text: A match is normally the best of five games, but may be the best of three
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 2.3

points.text: A return is good if it is struck before the ball bounces twice and reaches the front wall above the tin and below the out-line without first touching the floor or either player; it may hit other walls on the way
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 6.2

points.text: After a reasonable follow-through, each player must try to get out of the way so the opponent has a fair view of the ball, access to it, room to swing, and freedom to hit to any part of the front wall
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 8.1

points.text: A player who is obstructed may stop and ask for a let; the referee then allows a let, awards a stroke (the rally) to the striker, or allows nothing, depending on whether a good return was possible and whether the opponent tried to clear
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rules 8.2 and 8.6

points.text: A player loses the rally if their return touches the tin, goes out, or reaches the front wall only after bouncing on the floor
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 6.2

points.text: A player who lets the ball bounce twice on the floor before striking it loses the rally
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 6.2.1

points.text: If the ball hits the striker on its way back from the front wall and there was no interference, the opponent wins the rally
points.citation: World Squash Singles Rules 2025 V1.2, Rule 9.2.3

seo.title: Squash rules explained
seo.description: How squash is played: the serve, rally scoring to 11, lets and strokes, from the World Squash Singles Rules.

name: Badminton rules summary
summary: Badminton is played by two players or two pairs who hit a shuttle over a net and try to make it land inside the opponents' court. Every rally scores a point: a game goes to 21, with a two-point lead needed from 20-all and a cap at 30, and a match is the best of three games.

points.text: The serve is hit upwards over the net into the diagonally opposite service court, with the whole shuttle below 1.15 m from the court surface at the moment the racket strikes it
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 9.1 and 9.1.6

points.text: Server and receiver stand inside diagonally opposite service courts without touching the lines, with part of both feet in contact with the floor and stationary until the serve is struck
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 9.1.3 and 9.1.4

points.text: The server must hit the base of the shuttle first, without spinning it on release, and the racket must keep moving forwards once the service motion starts
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 9.1.5 and 9.1.7

points.text: In singles the server serves from the right service court when their score is zero or even, and from the left when it is odd
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 10.1.1 and 10.1.2

points.text: An incorrect serve is a fault, and a fault loses the rally to the other side
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 7.3 and 13

points.text: The side that wins a rally adds a point, whether or not it served; winning a rally as the receiver also wins the serve
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 7.3 and 10.3

points.text: A game is won by the first side to 21 points; from 20-all a side must lead by two, and at 29-all the next point wins
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Law 7

points.text: A match is the best of three games unless arranged otherwise, and the winner of a game serves first in the next
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Law 7

points.text: Players change ends after each game and, in a third game, when the leading side first reaches 11 points
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Law 8.1

points.text: It is a fault if the shuttle lands outside the court boundaries, fails to cross the net, touches the ceiling or side walls, or touches a player's body or clothing
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Law 13.3

points.text: It is a fault if the same player hits the shuttle twice in a row, or if partners hit it one after the other
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 13.3.7 and 13.3.8

points.text: While the shuttle is in play, a player must not touch the net or its supports, or reach over the net into the opponent's court (except to follow through after hitting the shuttle on their own side)
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 13.4.1 and 13.4.2

points.text: In doubles the serving side serves from the right service court when its score is zero or even and from the left when it is odd; the receiver is whichever opponent stands diagonally opposite
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Laws 11.1.1, 11.1.2 and 11.1.4

points.text: Partners only swap service courts when they win a point on their own serve
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Law 11.1.5

points.text: Once the serve is returned, either player on each side may hit the shuttle, from anywhere on their side of the net
points.citation: Laws of Badminton V5.0 (2), 26 April 2025, Law 11

seo.title: Badminton rules explained
seo.description: How badminton is played: the serve, rally scoring to 21, faults and doubles, from the BWF Laws of Badminton.

name: Table tennis rules summary
summary: Table tennis is played by two players or two pairs across a table divided by a net: the ball must bounce once on the opponent's half after each stroke. Every rally scores, a game goes to 11 with a two-point lead needed from 10-all, and a match is the best of an odd number of games.

points.text: The server rests the ball on the open palm of a still free hand, throws it almost straight up without spin so that it rises at least 16 cm, and strikes it on the way down so it bounces first on their own half and then on the receiver's
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Laws 2.6.1 to 2.6.3

points.text: From the start of the serve until it is struck, the ball must stay above the playing surface and behind the server's end line, and must not be hidden from the receiver by the server, their partner or their clothing
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.6.4

points.text: In doubles the serve must bounce first in the server's right half-court and then in the receiver's right half-court
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.6.3

points.text: A serve that touches the net assembly but is otherwise correct is a let and is taken again
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.9.1.1

points.text: Each player serves two points in turn; from 10-all, each player serves just one point in turn
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.13.3

points.text: Unless the rally is a let, a point goes to the player whose opponent fails to make a correct serve or return
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Laws 2.10.1.1 and 2.10.1.2

points.text: A game is won by the first player or pair to 11 points, unless both reach 10, in which case the first to lead by two points wins
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.11.1

points.text: A match is the best of any odd number of games
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.12.1

points.text: Players change ends after each game, and in the last possible game of a match when one side first reaches 5 points
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.13.7

points.text: After the serve, each return must be struck so that the ball lands on the opponent's court, either directly or after touching the net assembly
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.7.1

points.text: In singles the players hit alternately; in doubles the server, receiver, server's partner and receiver's partner hit in that order throughout the rally
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Laws 2.8.1 and 2.8.2

points.text: A player loses the point if, while the ball is in play, they or anything they wear or carry move the playing surface or touch the net assembly, or if their free hand touches the playing surface
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Laws 2.10.1.9 to 2.10.1.11

points.text: A player loses the point by obstructing the ball or by deliberately striking it more than once in succession
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Laws 2.10.1.6 and 2.10.1.7

points.text: A doubles player who hits the ball out of the order set by the first server and first receiver loses the point
points.citation: ITTF Statutes 2026, Laws of Table Tennis, Law 2.10.1.12

seo.title: Table tennis rules explained
seo.description: How table tennis is played: the serve, scoring to 11, the order of play and lost points, from the ITTF Laws of Table Tennis.

name: Pickleball rules summary
summary: Pickleball is played as singles or doubles on a small court with paddles and a perforated plastic ball. The serve goes diagonally across the net, and the serve and its return must each bounce before being hit. In standard scoring only the serving side scores, and a game is typically won by the first to 11 points with a two-point lead.

points.text: The serve goes to the service court diagonally opposite and must clear the non-volley zone (the area next to the net), with or without touching the net, and land in the correct service court
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 7.E

points.text: When the serve is hit, at least one of the server's feet must be on the playing surface inside the correct serving area behind the baseline, and neither foot may touch the court
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rules 7.A.1 to 7.A.3

points.text: For a volley serve, the paddle must move in a clear upward arc, its head must not be above the server's wrist, and the ball must be no higher than the waist at contact
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rules 7.C.1 to 7.C.3

points.text: A drop serve is also allowed: the server drops the ball from a natural height without propelling it and hits it after it bounces, however many times and wherever it bounces
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 7.D

points.text: A serve that lands outside the correct service court, lands in the non-volley zone, or hits a permanent object before landing is a fault against the server
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rules 7.E.1 to 7.E.3

points.text: In standard scoring, a point is scored only by the side that serves and wins the rally
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 4.A

points.text: A game is typically won by the first player or team to 11 points with a lead of at least two
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Section 1

points.text: In singles, the server serves from the right when their score is zero or even and from the left when it is odd, switching sides after each point won until they lose a rally
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rules 5.A.1 and 5.A.2

points.text: Rally scoring, in which the winner of every rally scores, is a provisionally approved option
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 14.A

points.text: Two-bounce rule: the serve and the return of serve must each bounce before they are hit
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 10.A

points.text: Players must return the ball before it bounces a second time
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 10.B

points.text: A volley (hitting the ball before it bounces) must be started outside the non-volley zone, the area within 2.13 m of the net on each side (given as 7 ft); touching the zone while volleying, or being carried into it by the momentum of a volley, is a fault
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rules 3.A.4.c, 11.A, 11.A.1 and 11.A.2

points.text: It is a fault if a player hits the ball out of bounds or fails to get it over the net
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rules 10.C.1 and 10.C.2

points.text: After the serve, it is a fault against a player if the ball touches them or anything they wear or carry, other than the paddle or the paddle hand below the wrist
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 10.C.3

points.text: A player may only call non-volley zone faults and service foot faults on an opponent; other suspected faults can be mentioned after the rally, but the player concerned decides
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rules 9.B.3 and 9.B.4

points.text: In doubles both partners serve before the serve passes to the other team, except at the start of each game, when only one player of the starting team serves
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 5.B

points.text: Serving and receiving positions follow the team's score: the starting server is on the right when the team's score is zero or even and on the left when it is odd
points.citation: 2026 USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, Rule 5.B.3

seo.title: Pickleball rules explained
seo.description: How pickleball is played: the serve, the two-bounce rule, the non-volley zone and side-out scoring, from the USA Pickleball rulebook.

name: Racquetball rules summary
summary: Racquetball is played by two or four players in an enclosed court where every wall and the ceiling can be used: each shot must reach the front wall before it touches the floor, and the ball may bounce only once before it is returned. Under IRF rules both sides can score, every game goes to 11 with a two-point lead, and a match is the best of five games.

points.text: The server bounces the ball on the floor inside the service zone and strikes it before it bounces again; the ball must hit the front wall first and then land beyond the back edge of the short line, with or without touching one side wall
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 3.3

points.text: The server has two attempts to put the ball in play; two fault serves in a row end that server's turn (a side-out in singles)
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rules 3.1, 3.6(b) and 3.11(a)

points.text: Fault serves include a short serve (landing on or in front of the short line), a serve that hits both side walls, the ceiling or the back wall before the floor, and starting the serve without both feet in the service zone
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 3.8

points.text: Some serves are an immediate out, with no second attempt: missing the ball completely, a serve that first hits anything other than the front wall, or a serve that rebounds and touches the server
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 3.9

points.text: The receiver must not enter the safety zone behind the short line until the served ball bounces or crosses the receiving line
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 3.10(b)

points.text: Points can be scored by either the serving or the receiving side
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 1.4

points.text: A match is won by the first player or team to win three games out of five
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 1.5

points.text: All games, including the tiebreaker, are played to 11 points, must be won by two points, and have no points cap
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 1.5

points.text: A return must be hit before the ball bounces twice and must reach the front wall before touching the floor; on the way it may touch the side walls, the ceiling or the back wall below the out-of-court line
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rules 1.3 and 3.10(c)

points.text: Only the head of the racquet may be used to hit the ball, held in one or both hands, and the ball may be struck only once per return
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rules 3.12(a) and 3.12(b)

points.text: A player fails to make a legal return, and loses the rally, if the ball bounces twice, does not reach the front wall on the fly, or touches their body or clothing
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 3.12(c)

points.text: Switching hands during a rally, or playing without the racquet's wrist safety cord, also loses the rally
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rules 3.12(a) and 3.12(c)

points.text: If the serving side loses a rally it loses the serve and the receivers score a point; if the receiving side loses it, the servers score
points.citation: IRF Official Rules 2026-2028 (March 2026), Rule 3.12(d)

seo.title: Racquetball rules explained
seo.description: How racquetball is played: the serve, scoring to 11, the walls and lost rallies, from the IRF Official Rules.

name: Platform tennis rules summary
summary: Platform tennis is a doubles game played outdoors on a small raised court enclosed by wire screens: the ball may be played off the screens after it bounces inside the court. Scoring follows tennis, with games, sets and tiebreakers, but each server gets only one serve.

points.text: The server stands behind the baseline between the centre mark and the sideline, throws the ball up by hand and hits it before it lands; the serve may be overarm, underarm or sidearm and must land in the diagonally opposite service court
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rules 9a, 9d and 9f

points.text: Only one serve is allowed in doubles: a service fault loses the point
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 9g

points.text: There are no service lets: a serve that clips the net cord and lands in the correct service court is in play
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 9h

points.text: The receiver must let the serve bounce; volleying it loses the point outright
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 10d

points.text: If the serve hits either receiver, or anything they wear or carry, before it bounces, the server wins the point
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 9i

points.text: Games are scored love, 15, 30, 40, game; from deuce a team must win two points in a row
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 6a

points.text: A set goes to the first team to win 6 games with a two-game lead; at 6-all a 7-point tiebreaker is normally played
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rules 6b and 6d

points.text: A match is usually the best of three sets; in some events a 10-point match tiebreaker replaces the third set
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rules 6c and 6d

points.text: Once the ball has bounced inside the court it stays in play off the screens until it bounces a second time, lands out, or goes over the screen; a ball that hits the screen before bouncing is out of play
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 11

points.text: A team loses the point if its shot lands in, rebounds off the back screen or corner, and comes back over the net to the hitter's side without the opponents touching it; this does not apply to the serve
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 14n

points.text: Hitting the ball over the screen and out of the enclosure, or into a light or the netting above the cross bar, loses the point
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 14m

points.text: A serve is a fault if the server stands in the wrong place or foot-faults, misses the ball, or the serve lands outside the correct service court or hits the server's partner
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rule 9j

points.text: A team loses the point if the ball bounces twice on its side, or if its return lands outside the court on the other side of the net
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rules 14a and 14b

points.text: A player loses the point if the ball touches them or their clothing, if they touch the net or posts while the ball is in play, or if both partners hit the ball on the same return
points.citation: APTA Official Rules of Platform Tennis (web page), Rules 14g, 14i and 14j

seo.title: Platform tennis rules explained
seo.description: How platform tennis is played: the single serve, scoring, the screens and lost points, from the APTA Official Rules.

name: Soft tennis rules summary
summary: Soft tennis is played mainly as doubles on a tennis-style court: pairs hit the ball over the net after at most one bounce. A game goes to the first pair to win four points (with deuce at three-all), and a match is usually decided over seven or nine games, with a final game played to seven points.

points.text: The server tosses the ball up by hand and strikes it before it lands, from behind the baseline between the imaginary extensions of the centre mark and the sideline
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Articles 20 and 23

points.text: The serve goes into the diagonally opposite service court, starting from the right of the centre mark and then alternating left and right
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 24.1

points.text: Each server serves two points in a row in turn, and the order of serving cannot change during a game
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 24.2

points.text: If the first serve is a fault the server has a second serve; two faults in a row lose the point
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Articles 25.2 and 27

points.text: A serve that touches the net or post and then lands in the correct service court is a let and is taken again
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 26

points.text: A game is won by the first pair to win four points; at three points each the score is deuce, and a pair must then win two points in a row
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 18.1

points.text: Matches are played over 7 or 9 games in principle; shorter formats (a 15-point match, or 3 or 5 games) and set-based formats are also allowed
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 17

points.text: If the games are level before the last one (for example 3-3 in a seven-game match), a final game is played: the first pair to 7 points wins, with deuce at six-all
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 18.2

points.text: Serving changes hands after each game, except in the final game, where the serve passes every two points
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 32

points.text: A serve is a fault if it does not land directly in the correct service court, if the server tosses the ball but does not strike it, or if the server foot-faults by touching the baseline, sideline or centre mark or stepping into the court
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 25.1

points.text: The receiving side loses the point if the receiver fails to return the serve legally, if the serve hits the receiver directly, or if it hits the receiver's partner before its second bounce
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 30

points.text: In a rally a player loses the point if they fail to hit the ball before its second bounce, or if their shot does not cross the net or lands outside the court
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 35.1

points.text: A player also loses the point if the ball touches their body or clothing, if they touch the net or post, or if the ball touches the racket more than once in a stroke
points.citation: ISTF Technical Rules (doubles), Article 35.1

seo.title: Soft tennis rules explained
seo.description: How soft tennis is played: the serve, four-point games, the final game and lost points, from the ISTF Technical Rules.

name: Beach tennis rules summary
summary: Beach tennis is played on sand, usually as doubles, and the ball is never allowed to bounce: every shot must be hit in the air and sent over the net into the opponents' court. Games use tennis scoring with a deciding point at deuce, sets go to six games, and a match tie-break to ten points replaces a third set.

points.text: The server stands at rest behind the baseline, within the sidelines extended, releases the ball by hand in any direction and hits it before it touches the ground
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rule 17
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: There is no second serve, and in mixed doubles the men must serve underarm
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rule 18
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: A serve that touches the net or band and carries on over the net is in play; there is no service let
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rule 22
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: Both teams must stay out of the prohibited service return zone, which runs 3.0 m back from the net on each side, until the serve has been hit
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rule 9 and Appendix I
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: The serve is a fault if the server foot-faults, misses the ball, or the ball hits a permanent fixture, the net post, the server or the server's partner
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rules 19 and 20
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: Games are scored love, 15, 30, 40, game; at deuce one deciding point is played (no advantage)
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rule 8a
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: A set goes to the first team to win six games with a two-game lead; at six games all a tie-break game to seven points is played
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rules 7 and 8b
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: A match is the best of three sets, but at one set all a match tie-break to ten points, with a two-point lead, replaces the final set
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rules 6 and 7
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: A team loses the point if the ball touches the ground inside the court on its side of the net, so every shot must be played in the air
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rule 24b
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: A team loses the point if its return lands outside the correct court or hits a permanent fixture or the net post before landing
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rules 24c and 24d
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: A player loses the point by touching the net, the posts or the opponents' court while the ball is in play, by hitting the ball before it crosses the net, or if the ball touches them or anything they wear or carry other than their racket
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rules 24f, 24g and 24h
points.editorNote: Read 2026-10-25 from a copy of the official PDF downloaded from itftennis.com on 2026-10-24; a fresh download on 2026-10-25 was blocked by the site's bot check. The ITF 2026 amendments only change Appendix II (rackets) for beach tennis.

points.text: A team also loses the point if both partners touch the ball on the same return
points.citation: ITF Rules of Beach Tennis 2023, Rule 24j
